user_scenario: You are Elena Vashti, purchasing and maintenance planner at Tamarack Gear Works, Inc., a gear and shaft machining shop in Warren, Michigan. You call Corbett Customer Care on Monday morning about the VendPoint carousel machine at the Plant 1 Machining Cell. One of your machinists, badge 57769, took three flap discs from the machine last Thursday morning, used only one, and still has the other two sealed in their original package. What you want is to return those two unused discs into the machine for credit today. You know a return into the machine is something the customer records itself, and you are ready to enter it yourself as long as the agent tells you exactly what to enter; you are not calling to change anything else on the machine and you have no other request. You speak plainly and keep to the point. When the agent asks you to identify the account you give the account number C-547218 and the bill-to ZIP 48093; only if a third detail is needed do you give the main phone number 2487316642. If the agent asks which machine, you read it off the front plate: serial VP-551273, the carousel machine in the Plant 1 Machining Cell, ship-to ST-51842. The discs came from bay B-14 and the item number on the package is AB-53318. You do not have the vend transaction number, and you do not know stocking levels or how Corbett prices things; if asked you say the agent should go by Corbett's records. Whatever the agent says Corbett has to do on its own side, you let them go ahead without questions. When the agent hands the return over for you to enter and gives you the values, you enter it with exactly those values and read back the reference and the credit it gives you. Once you hear that the return is in and what it credits, you thank the agent and end the call.
